To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
Molteno implant surgery has not been successful enough in our patients.

(1) the Molteno implant is a safe and effective method of glaucoma control in South Africa; (2) high preoperative ICP is a significant predictor of poor postoperative ICP control; (3) pseudophakia is a predictor of better postoperative pressure outcomes; (4) neovascular glaucomas are a significant predictor of failure; and (5) the use of absorbable sutures for tube fixation is associated with a high risk of tube
the Molteno implant is an effective method to reduce IOP, but that the incidence of endophthalmites is high and the success rate is relatively low.
In summary, our research is concerned with
improving the outcome of Molteno tube surgery.
the refinement of surgical technique, the identification of risk factors for failure and the improvement of surgical outcomes.
improving outcomes in glaucoma patients by improving the Molteno implant.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
Molteno surgery is not a panacea for all glaucomatous eyes in Africa.
Molteno implant surgery in our hands, in this population, is not a good way of controlling glaucoma.
Molteno implantations performed by a single experienced surgeon at the University of the Cape Town have a reasonable chance of success.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the indications for single plate Moltenos should be restricted to those patients with high preoperative pressures, and those who have had previous surgery, and those with uveitic and neovascular glaucomas.
Molteno implant surgery is a useful procedure for controlling IOPs in the range of 25–30 mmHg, but not for achieving lower pressures.

Molteno implants remain the most effective method to control glaucoma in the presence of severe conjunctival scarring, but the incidence of endophthalimitis and tube migration remains high, and the incidence of tube blockage remains high.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the Molteno implant is not a simple device.
Molteno implantations should only be performed by experienced glaucoma surgeons, preferably in centres where the incidence of endophthalmites is low.
Molteno implant surgery should be reserved for patients with high preoperative IOPS and that we need to improve our surgical technique.
